Financial Accounting and Financial
Statement Analysis
Why This Course
Understanding the financial health and performance of a business is essential for every manager
and decision-maker. This course introduces the principles and practices of financial accounting
and enables students to interpret and analyze financial statements with confidence. By learning
how to read income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements, students will gain
insight into a company's financial condition and its strategic choices. Additionally, through ratio
analysis and exposure to real-life financial reports, the course prepares students to make
informed decisions based on financial data.
This foundational knowledge is indispensable for anyone aiming to work in corporate roles,
finance, consulting, equity analysis, or entrepreneurship.
Pre-requisites (if any): None
Competencies This Course Develops
• Understanding and application of key accounting concepts and rules
• Interpretation of income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements
• Ability to perform detailed financial statement analysis using various financial ratios
• Preparation and interpretation of cash flow statements from operations, investing, and
financing activities
• Familiarity with ESG-linked financial reporting and key Indian accounting standards
• Exposure to management accounting fundamentals including cost behaviour and break-
even analysis

Corporate Finance
Why Take This Course?
Finance is often referred to as the language of business – it helps us translate strategy into
numbers, risk into measurable outcomes, and investment into value. Every business decision
has financial implications, whether it’s launching a new product, acquiring a competitor, or
deciding how much to distribute as dividends. This course lays the foundation for understanding
how finance drives business decisions.
Corporate Finance is a core course that equips you with the essential tools and conceptual
frameworks needed to understand how businesses raise capital, allocate resources, and create
value. Whether you are aspiring to be a strategy consultant, investment banker, entrepreneur, or
a corporate manager, this course helps you understand how the world of money operates within
a corporation.
Pre-requisites (if any): NA
Competencies Developed in This Course
1. Build a strong foundation in financial decision-making and its implications for business.
2. Apply time value of money concepts to real-world business problems.
3. Analyze investment opportunities using capital budgeting techniques.
4. Understand and evaluate risk-return trade-offs using financial models.
5. Value bonds and equities using appropriate financial valuation techniques.
6. Develop a nuanced view of working capital needs and their management.
7. Critically evaluate corporate financing choices and dividend policies.
Relevance and Career Linkages

Economics for Business
Why This Course
This course provides a structured way to analyze how individuals, firms, and governments make
choices under resource constraints. Whether it is setting prices, entering new markets, managing costs,
or responding to policy changes, economic principles guide rational and strategic business decisions.
This course grounds students in the fundamentals of microeconomics and macroeconomics, equipping
them to: understand firm behaviour under different market structures, analyze cost behaviour and
production efficiency, evaluate the impact of economic policies on business outcomes, interpret key
economic indicators to anticipate changes in demand, inflation, and interest rates, and apply concepts
like elasticity, marginal analysis, and opportunity cost in everyday business contexts.
By the end of the course, students will possess an economist’s toolkit to make informed, data-driven
decisions aligned with both firm-level goals and broader economic forces.
Pre-requisites (if any): None
Competencies this course develops
1. Apply microeconomic concepts such as demand, elasticity, production, and cost to business
decision-making
2. Understand different market structures and pricing strategies
3. Evaluate the impact of macroeconomic factors like inflation, interest rates, and fiscal policy
on business operations
4. Strengthen critical thinking through real-world case studies and application-based problem-
solving
5. Communicate economic reasoning effectively in a business context

Organizational Behaviour and Human
Resource Management
Why This Course:
Understanding people is at the heart of building successful organizations. This course explores
how individuals and teams behave within organizations and how HR systems influence those
behaviors. It integrates foundational concepts of Organizational Behaviour—like personality,
motivation, and leadership—with core HRM practices such as recruitment, performance
management, and compensation. The course emphasizes applying these principles in today’s
complex work environments shaped by technology, diversity, and ESG imperatives. By linking
OB theories with real-world HRM systems, students learn to design people-centric strategies
that improve collaboration, employee experience, and organizational effectiveness. This course
builds a solid base for those aspiring to shape work cultures and manage human capital in
dynamic and ethical ways.
Pre-requisites (if any): None
Competencies this course develops include ability to:
• Understand and analyze individual and group behaviour in workplace settings
• Apply OB concepts to leadership, motivation, and organizational change
• Evaluate and design key HRM systems like recruitment, performance, and rewards
• Integrate OB and HRM for strategic talent and culture decisions
• Interpret the role of ESG, DEI, and digital transformation in managing people
• Use a people-first lens to solve organizational challenges

Business Strategy and Simulations
Why This Course
This course provides a dynamic and experiential approach to understanding how firms develop,
execute, and adjust business strategies to achieve sustainable competitive advantage. Through
the integration of business simulations and strategy frameworks, students will act as executive
decision makers managing firms in competitive, uncertain environments. The course bridges
theory and practice—covering environmental analysis, strategic planning, cross-functional
integration, and real-time decision making—while emphasizing critical thinking, teamwork, and
leadership. Students will gain actionable insights into the interplay of marketing, operations,
finance, HR, and technology in driving firm performance and value creation. The simulated
environment allows risk-free experimentation with business decisions, preparing students for
complex strategic challenges in real organizations.
Pre-requisites: None
Competencies this course develops
• Applying strategic management concepts and analytical tools in simulated business
scenarios
• Crafting, implementing, and adapting business-level and corporate-level strategies
• Making cross-functional decisions with an understanding of their impact on overall
firm performance
• Integrating market analysis, financial planning, operations, and human resource
management in strategy execution
• Leading teams, managing conflict, and communicating strategic plans and outcomes
effectively
• Leveraging digital tools and data analytics for strategic planning and performance
measurement

Managerial Decision Making
Why This Course
In an increasingly data-driven business environment, effective decision-making is crucial for
organizational success. This course equips students with analytical frameworks and statistical
tools to make informed, data-backed managerial decisions. By blending decision science with
practical business applications, students learn how to navigate uncertainty, analyze complex
problems, and derive actionable strategies.
Pre-requisites (if any): None (Basic understanding of quantitative methods is helpful).
Competencies this course develops
• Decision Science Fundamentals – Mastering core principles of decision-making, data-
driven strategies, and analytics governance.
• Descriptive Analytics – Understanding data measurement scales, central tendency,
and variability to summarize business data.
• Probability & Sampling – Applying probability distributions (Normal & Standard
Normal) and sampling techniques to assess business scenarios.
• Hypothesis Testing & Confidence Intervals – Conducting z-tests, t-tests, Chi-square
tests, and ANOVA to support managerial decisions.
• Regression & Correlation – Building bivariate and multiple regression models to
identify patterns, relationships, and predictive insights.
• Ethical Decision-Making – Emphasizing accountability, transparency, and governance
in the deployment of analytical models.
• Capstone Applications – Solving real-world business cases from industries like retail
and banking using Excel and statistical tools.

Operations Management
Why This Course
Efficient operations are the backbone of any successful organization. This course provides
students with the tools and techniques to design, manage, and optimize processes that
enhance business performance. Covering topics such as process analysis, lean principles,
inventory control, and sustainable operations, students will learn how to address complex
operational challenges in a dynamic, globalized business environment.
Pre-requisites (if any): None.
Competencies this course develops
• Foundations of Operations Management – Process mapping, bottleneck analysis,
cycle time, and efficiency improvements.
• Production and Service Systems – Workload balancing, queuing models, and
performance optimization.
• Inventory Management – EOQ, safety stock, ABC classification, and managing
perishable inventory.
• Variability and Quality Control – Statistical process control, process capability
analysis, and quality metrics.
• Revenue and Operations Strategy – Pricing, capacity allocation, and aligning
operations with business strategy.
• Supply Chain & Sustainability – Network design, logistics models, and circular
economy practices for sustainable growth.

Social Immersion Programme
Why This Course
The Social Immersion Programme (SIP) is essential for developing empathy and tolerance by
immersing students in real-world social contexts, especially among underprivileged
communities different from their own. It fosters a deep sense of social responsibility and
awareness, sensitizing students to diverse lived realities and challenges. By integrating
experiential learning with reflective practices, SIP cultivates critical ethical understanding and
promotes sustainable, community-centered problem-solving skills. This immersive experience
nurtures socially conscious leaders equipped to engage compassionately and effectively in a
globalized society while appreciating contextual differences.
Pre-requisites: Course on Introduction to Sustainability
Competencies this course develops
1. Empathy and Social Awareness: Students learn to value and understand individuals
living differently from themselves, especially those from marginalized backgrounds,
fostering genuine empathy and social sensitivity.
2. Tolerance: Immersion builds openness to people with different life experiences and
contexts, strengthening tolerance and intercultural respect.
3. Problem Identification and Analytical Skills: Through direct engagement with social
issues, students develop discernment in problem framing, situation analysis, and the

focusing on four key pillars: self-awareness, emotional resilience, wellness, and professional

Using diagnostic assessments and experiential learning activities, Level 0 facilitates the

1. Mastering professional etiquette, discipline, and responsible behavior

Industry Internship Program
Why This Course
The Industry Internship Program bridges classroom learning with real world business practice.
Serving as a capstone course, the IIP immerses students in a corporate environment for three
months, where they tackle authentic business challenges. Students partner with organizations
to address substantive problems, applying analytical frameworks, strategic thinking, and
multidisciplinary knowledge gained through their program. Faculty guidance and structured
feedback ensure a focus on continuous improvement and professional growth. This experience
cultivates confidence, practical insights, and a strong foundation for career advancement
across disciplines.
Pre-requisites: None (Eligibility as per IIP policy; typically undertaken at the advanced stage of
the program)
Competencies this course develops
• Deconstructing and framing organizational problems using data and structured analysis
• Evaluating alternatives, synthesizing insights, and presenting feasible solutions that
satisfy stakeholders across functions
• Engaging in rigorous primary and secondary research to support actionable
recommendations
• Strengthening oral and written communication skills through reports, presentations,
and professional documentation
• Navigating teamwork, managing client relationships, and demonstrating business
professionalism in a real-world context
Applicable for all students irrespective of major area.

Introduction to Python Programming

Python has become the go-to programming language for data analytics, machine learning, and
automation, surpassing traditional tools like Excel for scalable and robust business solutions.
This course introduces students to the fundamentals of Python programming with a focus on
data manipulation and visualization. Through hands-on practice with libraries like NumPy,
pandas, and seaborn, students will learn to analyze real-world datasets and generate
actionable insights for data-driven decision-making.
Pre-requisites (if any): None.
Competencies this course develops
• Python Basics – Mastering data types, variables, operators, control statements, loops,
and file handling.
• Data Structures & Functions – Working with strings, lists, tuples, dictionaries,
modules, and functions.
• Data Manipulation – Using NumPy arrays, pandas Series, and DataFrames for data
